full_judgment:
7. Mr Ziaul Hasan, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submitted that opposite patty No, 1, knowing fully well that the petitioner's predecessors-in-interest were the proprietors of the trade mark "Red Cow", fraudulently applied to register the very same trademark in its own name, falsely claiming to be the proprietor. He submitted that the selfsame Nurul Islam, who is the proprietor of Sanowara Corporation as well as the Managing Director of Unilac Sanowara (BD) Ltd, entered into the Agency Agreement on behalf of Sanowara Corporation admitting the petitioner's predecessor-in-interest as the proprietor of the trademark "Red Cow" in the year 1986 and subsequently, in the year 1999, falsely claimed himself to be proprietor of the same trademark. Learned Counsel pointed out that the claim by Nurul Islam in his affidavit that he had been importing milk under the trademark "Red Cow" since 1978 is palpably false since he entered the Agency Agreement much later, in 1986. Learned Counsel submitted that as the application filed by Unilac Sanowara (BD) Ltd is based on a false representation that it was the proprietor of the mark since 1990, the registration of that mark is liable to be expunged on that ground of fraud alone. In this regard, learned Counsel referred to the decision in the case of Societe de Fabrication et de Distribution de Parfumerie et Cosmetique (DIPARCO) Societe Anonyme vs Deputy Registrar of Trade Marks, Government of Pakistan and another reported in PLD 1979 Karachi 83. He further pointed out that the application for registration, which was filed on 28-11-1999 before the Registrar of Trade Marks, clearly shows interpolation of the date of the applicant's proprietorship in the trademark. That interpolation of the date not having been authorised, the application is liable to be expunged. Learned Counsel further submitted that the impugned trademark being exactly the same as that of the petitioner, undoubtedly, there is likely to be confusion in the minds of the public who are liable to be deceived as to the origin and manufacture of the product, which is violative of sections 8(a) and 10(1) of the Act. He submitted that in the interest of the public and for the sake of maintaining purity of the Register the impugned, trademark should be expunged. In support, he has referred to the decision in the case of Messrs Kanshiram Surinderkumar a Firm vs Messrs Thakurdas Deoonmal Rohire and others reported in AIR 1982 Bombay 505. Learned Counsel further submitted that the application having been received at a time when the same mark had already been registered earlier, the Registrar of Trade Marks failed in his duty under Rule 23 of the Rules in allowing the impugned trademark to be registered. In this regard, he has referred to the decision in the case of Md Abu Taher Sikder vs Registrar of Trade Marks and, another reported in 11 BLT 194. Referring to Annexure-M of the petitioner's affidavit-in-reply dated 12-6-2003, he pointed out that in Money Suit No. 13 of 2002, which was later numbered as Money Suit No. 20 of 2002, the plaintiff, Nurul Islam filed a money suit against Unilac Australia Pty Ltd. In that suit, the plaintiff filed an application for attachment, which is marked Annexure-N. In the prayer portion of the said application (Annexure-N) the plaintiff prayed for attachment of the trademark "Red Cow in Can" belonging to the defendant, namely, Unilac Australia Pty. Ltd. He submitted that the opposite party No. I thus admitted the proprietorship of the petitioner's predecessor-in-interest in the trademark "Red Cow in Can". Learned Counsel further submitted that the petitioner through its predecessors has been marketing  its goods  in the Bangladeshi, market since 1986 by virtue of the Agency Agreement  with Sanowara Corporation executed in 1986 and therefore, the claim of the opposite party No.1 that the petitioner does not market any goods under the trademark, is not true. 

 16. Let tis see whether in the instant case the opposite party No. 1 has taken recourse to fraud in obtaining registration of the trademark "Red Cow" with the device of a "Cow". In its application it quite categorically stated that it is the proprietor of the trademark, be it since 1990 or 1998 (as there is interpolation of the date. The Agency agreement dated 1-7-1986 and the subsequent Agency Agreement dated 1-7-1991 show that Sanowara Corporation agreed to act as the selling agent and market the product supplied by the principal (Unilac Australia Pty. Ltd) under the brand name "Red Cow". Although it is not clearly spelt out whether Unilae Australia Pty. Ltd. has proprietary right over the trademark "Red Cow" or is simply supplying products branded "Red Cow", of which the proprietary interest may belong to someone else, the fact re- mains that Sanowara Corporation and the signatory to the agreement on behalf of Sanowara Corporation, namely Nurul Islam, were fully aware that the brand name "Red Cow" did not belong to Unilac Sanowara (BD) Ltd. Thus to that extent the statement that Unilac Sanowara (BD) Limited has had proprietorship over the trademark since 1990 or 1998 is not a true fact. Moreover, it appears from Annexures-H, I and J that the tinned milk under the mark "Red Cow" with the device of "Cow" is a product from Australia supplied by Unilac Australia Pty. Ltd and Annexure] specifically shows that the packeting of the "Red Cow" branded milk powder was done by Unilac, Sanowara (BD) Ltd. for Bon- lac Foods Limited. This, along with the admission by Nurul Islam in Money Suit No. 20 of 2002 that the defendant, namely Unilac Australia Pty Ltd, owns the trademark "Red Cow in Can" and the admission in his affidavit dated 25-11-2002, mentioned above, is, in my view, clear indication that the trademark "Red Cow" did not belong to Unilac Sanowara (BD) Ltd. To that extent the registration has been obtained by fraud. For the same reason the trademark cannot be allowed to remain as a registration under section 10(2) of tile Trade Marks Act. Accordingly, it is my view that the registration obtained under trademark registration No. C-62724 in Class-29 dated 28-11-1999 is liable to be expunged.
